QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_6

question.text: 'Kaveri Seed Category I AIF' invested in a start-up using weighted-average anti-dilution. Pre-round cap: 1,00,000 equity shares (founders' shares at INR 10 face/paid). Angel round: 30,000 preference shares at INR 10 each, conversion price INR 20. In the next round the company issues 25,000 new shares at INR 10. Total capital raised to date = INR 14.50 lakh; total shares issued = 1,30,000 (using book-value convention). What is the revised conversion price and approximate new conversion ratio?

explanation.text: The Logic: Weighted-average method: New conversion price = total capital raised / total shares issued = INR 14,50,000 / 1,30,000 = INR 11.15. Revised conversion ratio = old conversion price / new conversion price = 20 / 11.15 ≈ 1.79. So each preference share converts to ~1.79 equity shares instead of 1. The Trap: INR 10 is full-ratchet, not weighted. INR 20 ignores the dilution. INR 14.50 mistakes 'lakh' for rupees-per-share. Cross-Exam Context: This is the PDF's worked example adapted. XIX-C uses the same math. XIX-A Distributor does not compute anti-dilution. Manager's Pro-Tip: Broad-based weighted average (includes options in 'fully diluted' denominator) is even founder-friendlier than narrow-based. Negotiate broad-based at Series A — founders will push, but it's become the Indian VC market standard.
